newsitem.title: CHINA: China rubber seen strong on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: China rubber seen strong on speculative buying.

text.p: Chinese rubber futures have strengthened with speculative buyers flexing their muscles and manipulating the market despite over-supply fundamentals, traders said on Monday.
Rises in the rubber price on the Hainan Commodity Futures Exchange last week should flow into continued volatility in the short term, rubber futures traders said.
The key August 1997 contract on the exchange ended Friday at 11,065 yuan ($1,333) per tonne, after continual rises from 10,840 yuan at the beginning of last week.

Due to low spot prices, rubber producers were anxious to build short positions below 11,000 yuan per tonne, while the low prices also provided chances for buyers with ample capital to manipulate the market against fundamentals, traders said.
The price of physical rubber is around 9,800 yuan per tonne in China's major production area of Hainan, a tropical island province off China's southern coast, they said.
"Because of the two month interval between the July and the August contracts, speculative buyers have enough time to make the market," one trader said.
"Speculative buyers seem confident in their ability to buck fundamentals," another trader said.
"The two-month interval gave them flexibiliy either to lift prices to squeeze the shorts or to offset their positions at high levels," he said.
Traders said market risks had intensified due to the battle between the shorts and the longs. They said they expected to see some volatility on the rubber futures market in the short term.
"Though buyers performed well in the latest match, it would be wise to offset positions at high levels," one of the trading sources said.
"If shorts are pressed too tightly, they may strengthen their determination to battle with buyers," he said.
